verdict: Both panes are the same 368px column with the same hairline at x=733 and the same rules from x=91 to 704, so this comes down to ink, and A has more of it where you read: previews and dates a full step darker, rows on a rigid 75px grid instead of a 77/78 wobble. A then throws it away on the one control that matters — a search field whose label is 48 levels lighter than its own icon, so the first thing a writer does in a library of eight manuscripts is poke a field that looks switched off. B is the more consistent grey system and the less legible one; its previews are dimmed to 2.8:1 and it tells you your manuscripts live 'In this browser', which is not a sentence a novelist wants under their file list. Pick A and change one hex value; picking B means arguing every grey in the pane.

states.name: search
states.gap: No disclosure on the Location: the header reads 'library' with a folder icon and nothing else, where A shows 'Library ⌄' with a 7×27 logical px chevron 8 px after the label — B gives a writer no visible signal that the library folder is switchable or that the name is a control at all. Same header also drops to the lowercase raw directory name, so the pane is titled like a path fragment rather than a place.
states.gapTheirs: The library pane runs a second, paler grey than the rest of the app: every scanning-layer element inside it — date, two-line preview, '2 of 8 documents', 'Sort by Date', 'All changes saved' — is #999999 on a #FDFDFD panel (2.80:1), while the editor chrome 12 logical px away across the hairline (title 'sea-storm.md', '35 words / < 1 min read' labels) is #8C8C8C (B uses #8C8C8C in both places, 3.14:1). A compounds it by tinting the panel #FDFDFD against a #F9F9F9 page, so the file list is the brightest surface in the window and the manuscript the duller one, while holding the faintest text on screen.
states.verdict: These are twins — same 367 px column, same 16.5 px icon rail, same 46→353 px inset separators, same 4 px accent bar at ~87% of row height — so the choice comes down to which grey you stare at for a year. A makes the pane the whitest thing in the window and then prints the previews, dates and save status in the palest ink in the window at 2.80:1, one step lighter than the identical status text sitting beside it across the hairline; that mismatch is visible in the footer, where 'All changes saved' is demonstrably paler than '35 words' on the same baseline. B holds one paper (#F7F7F7 both sides) and one grey (#8C8C8C everywhere), which is what makes a file list scannable at a glance instead of squint-legible. B pays for it with a header that admits no way to change Location and a status line whose baseline sits 2 px below the word count on the same strip — annoying, but a chevron is one control, whereas A's grey is every row, every date, every session.
secondary: A panel #FDFDFD vs page #F9F9F9 (Δ4/255, hairline #E7E7E7); B panel and page both #F7F7F7 with only a #DFDFDF hairline — the pane sits on the theme's paper
A's sidebar footer baseline is within ~0.75 logical px of the editor word-count baseline; B's sits 2 logical px lower on the same strip
Row height A 78 vs B 74 logical px for the same two-line preview; selection tint delta identical (5 levels above pane bg in both)
Search-match chip near identical: #B6E8FD 24×18 vs #B2E7F9 23×19.5 logical, both darken the matched word to ~#1A1A1A, both ~0.5 px horizontal padding; A rounds the corner 1 px, B square
Both filter to '2 of 8 documents' on the query, so the search state is no differentiator
Footer copy: A 'In this browser' names where the manuscript actually lives; B 'On this device' is vaguer about the same browser storage — the trust-relevant sentence, and A's is the honest one
Neither offers a resize grip on the 367 px column, a scrollbar, or any rename/reveal affordance; ~1200 px of dead pane below the last row in both
Header insets: A left 15 / right 13.5 logical px (1.5 px asymmetric), B left 14 / right 14.5 (0.5 px)
